A piece of fabric attached to a boat and arranged such that it causes the wind to drive the boat along. The sail may be attached to the boat via a combination of mast, spars and ropes.

examples.text: When we haue laught to ſee the ſailes conceiue / And grow big bellied with the wanton winde; […]

glosses: The concept of a sail or sails, as if a substance.

examples.text: Take in sail: a storm is coming.

glosses: The power harnessed by a sail or sails, or the use of this power for travel or transport.
A trip in a boat, especially a sailboat.

examples.text: Let's go for a sail.

glosses: A sailing vessel; a vessel of any kind; a craft.

examples.text: Twenty sail were in sight.

"[…] The quay is upwards of 1,000 feet in length, and capable of accommodating more than 100 sail of traders; and there are generally a considerable number of vessels of from 40 to 300 tons burden, from various parts of the world, waiting to receive their cargoes."

glosses: The conning tower of a submarine.
The blade of a windmill.

examples.text: So furious had been the gusts, that high buildings in town had had the lead stripped off their roofs; and in the country, trees had been torn up, and sails of windmills carried away; and gloomy accounts had come in from the coast, of shipwreck and death.

glosses: A tower-like structure found on the dorsal (topside) surface of submarines.

Anything resembling a sail, such as a wing.

examples.text: Like an eagle […]soaring / / To weather his broad sails.

glosses: To be impelled or driven forward by the action of wind upon sails, as a ship on water; to be impelled on a body of water by steam or other power.

examples.text:
Fair ship, that from the Italian shore,
⁠Sailest the placid ocean-plains
⁠With my lost Arthur’s loved remains,

glosses: To move through or on the water; to swim, as a fish or a waterfowl.
To ride in a boat, especially a sailboat.
To set sail; to begin a voyage.

examples.text: We sail for Australia tomorrow.

glosses: To move briskly and gracefully through the air.

examples.text: As is a winged messenger of heaven, […] / When he bestrides the lazy pacing clouds, / And sails upon the bosom of the air.

glosses: To move briskly but sedately.

examples.text: The duchess sailed haughtily out of the room.

glosses: To deal out (cards) from a distance by impelling them across a surface.

examples.text: He would sit his hat across the room, and we would sail cards into it.
